title: Tested, not vibed: GTM writing evals
tagline: Testing which of the instructions behind AI-written GTM copy beat saying nothing, with a public suite anyone can re-run.
why: The pipeline writes every post, note and brief from a style guide of more than 100 guidance lines. As of 8 November 2026, none of them had been run against a no-guidance control (first-party check of the pipeline repo), so nobody can say which lines change the output.
mission: AO-EVAL-SUITE, a public, re-runnable eval suite for GTM agent writing, aimed at Alex's own rulebook. It screens failure types drawn from his review comments against a no-guidance control, then tests rule wordings only where the control fails. Alongside it, an audit of every rule and a backfill of debriefs for attended rooms that never got one.
destination: A pre-registered study published with its raw samples, grader code and agreement between graders, so a stranger can re-run it. The rulebook keeps only the rules that beat saying nothing, and the count of rules tested appears on this page as a metric. Anyone can check by re-running the suite.
showcase: Designing a behaviour eval the way a lab would (designed, not yet run): pre-registration before the first sample, a no-guidance control, yes/no graders and a rep count set for statistical power
Screening many failure types against the control first instead of hand-picking test cases, which removes author selection bias
Sizing a build by two budgets: the hours only Alex can give (decisions, labels, reads) and the hours agents can run overnight
Applying a method from software engineering (test the instruction against its absence first) to sales and marketing writing

decisions.decision: Adopt the testing method, not the borrowed skills: an instruction stays only if it beats saying nothing.
decisions.why: Imported skills were written for coding agents. The method transfers to writing, the wording doesn't.

decisions.decision: Screen many failure types against a control instead of hand-picking two test cases.
decisions.why: Picking the cases yourself biases the study, and two small cases make the whole result hang on chance.

decisions.decision: Backfilled debriefs feed only the private knowledge graph. Drafts, outreach and CRM records stay out of the backfill, and every backfilled claim is tagged as backfill (by design).
decisions.why: Rooms debriefed weeks later are useful context, but they shouldn't read as first-hand records.

decisions.decision: Make no claim of being first until the write-up publishes with its prior-art section.
decisions.why: A claim of being first is only as strong as the search behind it, and that search belongs in the public write-up.

decisions.decision: Plan signed off: five lanes run at once, with agents building and running the samples, and the study design approved ahead of the written pre-registration.
decisions.why: The proof has to be public before the end-of-year window, and the sampling runs overnight on agent hours, not Alex's.

open.question: Where AO-EVAL-SUITE lives: its own public repo, or a folder in an existing one.

risks.risk: The author wrote the rules, the failure cases and the grader, so a positive result could just be the author agreeing with himself.
risks.mitigation: By design: pre-registration before the first sample, yes/no checks graded by code where possible, a blind grader that never sees the style guide, raw samples published, and outside graders whose agreement is reported.

risks.risk: Backfilled debriefs written weeks after the event could read as fact to later runs.
risks.mitigation: By design, every backfilled claim is tagged as backfill, and nothing public is written from a backfilled event.

log.text: Sampling throughput measured: 100 of 100 samples in 150 seconds, about 2,400 an hour against a floor of 60, so the rate does not limit the study. The runner now retries silent empty outputs and logs each retry. Suite scaffolded and the pre-registration drafted.
Plan rewritten at full scale, claims checked against prior art and narrowed, and the plan signed off.
